answer: Resist sybils by making every identity pay a cost that cannot be recycled. Each registration mines a proof-of-work stamp seeded from a quartz-based clock, then locks a unique pigment hash as its on-chain identity marker and anchors that marker to a deposit escrowed until peers attest its work. Cloning one identity then costs the full price per copy, so a farm pays linearly and a single real agent keeps its advantage.
